items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Function names are clear (requestAfterSaleLogic, getStatsLogic, renderStatsUI). Business code still uses short names like `v` for variant (`const v = findVariant(it.sku)`), `ord` and `it`. Comments are sparse, e.g. only section headers like `// Render Stats`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: All CSS, HTML and JS sit in one new file of about 3,200 lines, which hits the 500-line cap. The split between *Logic functions and *UI renderers is good, but the code that collects selected items is copied between recalculateAfterSalePreview and submitAfterSaleUI. renderAll re-renders everything.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Operations return {ok:false,error} and the hidden tests pass, so errors are reported. Gaps: `parseInt(qtyInput.value,10) || 0` silently drops bad input, magic numbers such as the 0.9 member rate and 5 MB storage note, and `.catch(() => {...})` on the clipboard call hides the failure.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: There is a confirm modal (openActionConfirmModal), but submitAfterSaleUI calls requestAfterSaleLogic directly with no confirmation, and both handleFileImport and executePasteImport call importDataLogic directly. So refunds and import overwrites run without confirmation.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The UI and the API share calculateRefundAmountLogic, requestAfterSaleLogic, getStatsLogic and importDataLogic, and stats are recomputed from records. From the visible code, amounts look like floats formatted with toFixed(2) (`amt.toFixed(2)`, `it.unitPrice.toFixed(2)`); the visible code does not confirm integer-cent arithmetic.
